items.title: Live: Trump likely target of shooting at correspondents' dinner, top US official says
items.description: US Acting Attorney-General Todd Blanche says the shooter apprehended at the White House correspondents' dinner was likely targeting Donald Trump. Follow live.

items.title: How dinner with the president descended into chaos
items.description: Thousands of influential players in Washington filed into a ballroom with the US president. Then shots rang out.

items.title: Trump says shooter's 'manifesto' shows he was a 'sick guy'
items.description: Several US media outlets are reporting on the existence of the manifesto, which reportedly states the shooter wanted to target administration officials, and was sent to the suspect's family members just before the attack.

items.title: Trump was 'all set to really rip' into the media, but he's changed his tune
items.description: While the latest act of violence wasn't as close as Trump's brush with death in Butler, Pennsylvania, almost two years ago, it will no doubt revive some trauma for Trump and those closest to him.

items.title: 'Membership to nothing': The multi-million-dollar Wild West of rewards clubs
items.description: "Rewards clubs" have exploded in Australia, claiming to have given away hundreds of millions in prizes, but they operate with almost no legal scrutiny.

items.title: Israel demands residents evacuate villages in southern Lebanon
items.description: Israeli forces have demanded residents in seven villages north of Lebanon's Litani River to evacuate.

items.title: Treasury's impossible task: Prepare a budget as oil shock unfolds
items.description: Accompanying the oil shock unfolding in the Strait of Hormuz is a profound change in the way fiscal and monetary policymakers operate. And as the government prepares the budget, with the impact of the Iran war still unfolding, a recession may be ahead.

items.title: Trump is political kryptonite in Australia, but Albanese must walk the line
items.description: As Donald Trump's approval in Australia sinks, Anthony Albanese needs to walk a careful line: keep voters convinced of the merits of the alliance, while avoiding the impression he is being too reverential.

items.title: China's 'quirky' fix for property crisis rewards marathon runners
items.description: Local governments in China are offering marathon runners, AI experts and tennis players subsidies to purchase unwanted properties amid a lingering real estate downturn.

items.title: US allies turning to Japan for defence supplies as Iran War drags on
items.description: Australia's multi-billion-dollar deal with Japan for its future warships could set a template that will help Tokyo rapidly expand defence exports across Asia.

items.title: Sixteen dead in strikes as Ukraine marks 40 years since Chernobyl
items.description: Marking the anniversary, Volodymyr Zelenskyy warns that Russia is using "nuclear terrorism" as a weapon of war.

items.title: Street artist Peter Drew on why his 'Aussie' posters are still important

items.title: Australia to sell fleet of Bushmaster armoured vehicles to the Dutch
items.description: Australian Bushmaster armoured vehicles are being sent to the Netherlands following a request to Australia by the Dutch government.

items.title: Two-hour barrier smashed twice in history-making London Marathon
items.description: Kenya's Sabastian Sawe has become the first man to run a marathon in under two hours, winning the London Marathon with a time of 1:59:30.

items.title: How friendship with Russell Crowe led to an MMA fight
items.description: Bosch & Rockit filmmaker Tyler Atkins's latest feature put his stars through the wringer on camera, but held them with love behind the scenes.

items.title: Why women are getting less sleep than men — and what we can do about it

items.title: Quiz: Have you got the memory to beat our history quiz?

items.title: Veteran's advice after Anzac Day booing: Find your 'warrior spirit'
items.description: While condemnation has been swift after Indigenous elders were booed on Anzac Day, solutions to this type of racism seem harder to pin down. Elders have advice to share.

items.title: AI is helping rangers protect Victorian wildlife in a fraction of the time
items.description: A new AI tool will help Parks Victoria manage native and endangered species affected by natural disasters, including the summer bushfires, with the department making the technology available to everyone.

items.title: A narco-sub washed up near their village. Inside was a troubling clue to its origins

items.title: Hani Watson learned the importance of listening to her rogue bones and 'Nigel'

items.title: Dawson fights back tears after return as GWS edge Roos amid ARC drama

items.title: Manly's revival continues as Foran sets record, Panthers down Knights
items.description: Manly's revival under interim coach Kieran Foran has continued with a fourth straight win, as the Sea Eagles scored five tries in the second half to sink the Parramatta Eels.

items.title: What Ringo did after the Beatles stunned the music world and he's still doing it 56 years later
items.description: Ringo's childhood love of classic country still influences the new music that The Beatles's drummer makes.

items.title: Taylor avoids backing ASIO amid questions on ISIS-linked families
items.description: Government action needs to be taken to prevent a group of Australian families with links to former ISIS fighters from re-entering the country, Opposition Leader Angus Taylor says.
